faqs.q: How much does a Borzoi cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $1,200–$4,000 for a Borzoi puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Borzoi?
faqs.a: Budget $200–$400 per month for a Borzoi, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Large breeds cost more across every category — food portions, medication doses and professional services all scale with weight.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Borzoi?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($800–1,200), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($800–1,800 per year). Grooming adds $400–$1,200 annually for Borzois due to their coat type.

faqs.q: How much does a Borzoi cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Borzoi are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,500–$5,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Borzoi?
faqs.a: Borzois need brushing 3–4 times per week to prevent matting.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Borzois shed a lot?
faqs.a: Borzois have seasonal shedding — manageable with a consistent brushing routine.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Borzoi need?
faqs.a: A wide-tooth comb, pin brush, and detangling spray are the core tools for a Borzoi's long coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for complete at-home maintenance.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Borzoi?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Borzois that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Borzois easy to train?
faqs.a: Borzois are independent thinkers and can be challenging to train. They respond best to high-value rewards and clear, consistent criteria. A structured puppy class from week one is strongly recommended.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Borzoi?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Borzois. Clicker training with precise timing works well to mark the exact moment of correct behaviour. Avoid aversive methods — they increase anxiety and often create secondary behavioural problems.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Borzoi?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Borzoi?
faqs.a: Borzois can take longer to reach reliable obedience than easier-to-train breeds — expect 3–6 months of consistent daily training for solid basics. Their independent nature means results compound slowly but durably with patience.

faqs.q: What health problems do Borzois commonly have?
faqs.a: Borzois are most commonly associated with ear infections. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Borzois live?
faqs.a: Borzois have an average lifespan of 9–14 years. Larger breeds typically have shorter lifespans than smaller breeds. Maintaining a healthy weight and regular vet care are the most impactful factors for longevity.

faqs.q: Are Borzois prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Borzois have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Borzoi puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Borzoi puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Borzoi-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Borzois good with kids?
faqs.a: Borzois are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Borzois get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Borzois are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Borzois bark a lot?
faqs.a: Borzois tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Borzois good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Borzois are not ideally suited to apartments — their size and energy level need outdoor space and significant daily exercise. If you do have an apartment, plan for 60–90 minutes of outdoor exercise daily and consider doggy daycare for additional stimulation.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Borzoi need per day?
faqs.a: Borzois need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Borzois good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Borzois make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Borzoi doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Borzois often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Borzoi be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Borzoi depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A long-line is recommended as an intermediate step for several months.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Borzoi?
faqs.a: A Borzoi needs approximately 3–5 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Borzoi?
faqs.a: Adult Borzois should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds. For large and giant breeds, twice daily feeding also reduces the risk of bloat (GDV) compared to one large daily meal.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Borzoi?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Borzois benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Borzoi from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Large breeds should stay on a large-breed puppy formula until 18–24 months, then transition to an adult formula. Switching too early can disrupt joint development during the growth phase.

faqs.q: Is a Borzoi a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Borzois can be challenging for first-time owners due to their independent temperament. Prior dog experience or professional training classes from the start significantly improves outcomes. Research the breed thoroughly before committing.

faqs.q: Are Borzois good family dogs?
faqs.a: Borzois are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Borzois do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Borzois form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Borzoi?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Borzoi — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction. Add 15–30 minutes for grooming 3–4 times weekly. The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
